memory_update.text: AEP is a priority direct-regulated-utility candidate for the large_load_grid_interconnection node because AEP Ohio has an approved Data Center Tariff, a 2026 study tranche process, and reported 5,642 MW of binding data-center contracts.
Dominion Energy is a priority direct-regulated-utility candidate because Virginia data-center demand creates unusually high queue, transmission, and cost-allocation sensitivity inside PJM.
Exelon/ComEd is a strong second direct-utility candidate due to FERC-reviewed data-center transmission agreements and Exelon’s cited 18 GW high-probability data-center pipeline.

Xcel Energy should remain in the universe as a non-PJM large-load tariff exposure, useful for tracking whether state-level tariff frameworks become investable chokepoints outside the Mid-Atlantic data-center corridor.
Talen Energy is a direct IPP test case for hyperscaler power procurement under FERC/PJM co-located load rules; include with higher regulatory-risk labeling.

Future passes should separately test CEG, PWR, ETN, GEV, VST, PPL, PEG, NEE, AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META, and data-center REITs/operators for second-order exposure through co-location filings, transmission EPC, switchgear, utility-service territory demand, and secured interconnection rights.

PWR should remain a core Layer 1B candidate for large-load grid interconnection because it maps to the scarce execution layer: transmission EPC, substations, utility T&D, and large-load infrastructure buildout.

ETN and GEV represent scarce equipment buckets likely to gate post-approval energization: switchgear/power distribution, transformers, grid equipment, substations, HVDC, synchronous condensers and generation equipment.

AEP is a regulated-asset candidate where the upside/risk is strongly dependent on ESA quality, take-or-pay protections, cost allocation, state commission approvals and actual data-center load realization.

The node is not just physical transmission capacity; it combines regulatory permission, interconnection-study queues, financial security/deposits, cost-allocation rules, utility capex recovery, and long-lead equipment.

Potential follow-up candidates excluded due to the five-name limit: Dominion Energy for Northern Virginia transmission/data-center load; Constellation and Vistra for PJM co-located generation and nuclear PPAs; MasTec for transmission construction; Powell Industries for switchgear; Itron/OSI/GEV grid software for interconnection visibility and load control.

NiSource should be tracked as a less obvious utility/data-center power beneficiary because its NIPSCO GenCo structure is explicitly designed for large-load customers and has Alphabet/Amazon-linked evidence.
Portland General Electric has one of the clearest live tariff-framework case studies, with Oregon implementation beginning June 10, 2026 and disclosed contracted/requested data-center load.
AEP is a high-evidence large-load tariff and transmission candidate outside the seed universe, with AEP Ohio disclosing 5,642 MW of binding data-center contracts as of February 12, 2026.

Itron adds software/analytics/demand-response coverage to the node: large-load rules may increase the need for forecasting, grid-edge visibility, DERMS, and operational control rather than only physical transmission equipment.

Need a separate pass on publicly traded transmission/substation component suppliers such as Hubbell and electrical distributors, and on regional utilities with pending tariffs such as Xcel, PPL, Duke, Entergy, and Dominion.

node: Large-load grid interconnection and transmission rules
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded a focused US-listed universe for companies directly exposed to large-load interconnection, data-center tariffs, transmission queues, and co-located generation rules. The strongest direct exposures in this pass are regulated utilities with data-center-heavy service territories and formal tariff or queue processes, plus an IPP whose data-center nuclear supply model has already been shaped by FERC/PJM interconnection decisions. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation. Layer 1B expansion for the large-load grid interconnection node found five US-listed candidates with plausible direct or second-order exposure to the emerging scarcity around data-center grid access, PJM/FERC co-location rules, transmission cost allocation, and long-lead grid equipment. The most node-proximate public-market mappings in this pass are transmission/grid EPC capacity, scarce electrical equipment, grid-equipment OEMs, utility T&D components, and regulated utilities with executed large-load pipelines. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded universe for the large-load grid interconnection node, focused on second-order and potentially underappreciated beneficiaries of data-center-driven load growth, tariff reform, queue reform, transmission/substation upgrades, and utility planning software. The strongest mappings in this pass are regulated utilities with signed or approved large-load frameworks, plus suppliers that help utilities model, connect, and harden the grid. This is research support only and is not a buy/sell recommendation.
